22.0.0.en: Satan entered: through the lust of the love of money.

22.0.1.en: Of the number of the twelve: that is, one of those nearest to Christ, and this shows the heinousness of his sin.

22.0.2.en: The chief priests: the heads of the twenty-four divisions of the priests, in addition to the high priest and the former chief priests.

22.0.3.en: Captains: the commanders of the guard under the chief priests.

22.0.4.en: Judas Iscariot fell into the love of money. Although he was one of Christ's disciples, since he had the bag he used to steal from it, and then the love of money grew in his heart, so he wanted to sell Christ his Teacher and deliver Him to the Jews; so he went to the chief priests and agreed with them to betray Christ to them.

22.1.0.en: The chief priests rejoiced at his betrayal and promised to give him its price, thirty pieces of silver, which is the price of the compensation paid at the death of a slave if an ox gores him, for example (Ex 21:32). Thus Christ was sold at the price of a slave, the lowest of prices, and Judas accepted this agreement and began to look for an opportunity to find Christ away from the crowds in order to arrest Him.

22.1.1.en: The bitterness of betrayal is hard, so do not seek your own advantage before others', and what you would not want to happen to you, do not do to another.

22.2.0.en: Then came: drew near, since the next day, Friday, was the time of the Passover feast, so Christ did this on Thursday, a day before its time, so that He Himself would be our Passover when He was crucified on Friday at the time of the Passover feast. The Passover feast drew near, that is, the feast of Unleavened Bread, and so that He might fulfill all righteousness for us, He sent Peter and John to prepare the Passover for Him and His disciples according to the law of Moses.

22.3.1.en: The house: the house of St. Mark, where He ate the Passover and instituted the Lord's Supper after it.

22.3.2.en: The two disciples asked Christ about the place He chose to eat the Passover in, and He said to them that when they entered the city they would find a man carrying a pitcher of water, and to follow him until he entered a house, and to prepare the Passover there. This man was Mark the Apostle, according to the tradition of the Church.

22.3.3.en: The pitcher of water signifies Baptism, which a person must receive first and then enjoy the Body and Blood of the Lord (the Lord's Supper).

22.4.0.en: When you have entered the house, ask its owner, who is Mark the Apostle, where Christ and His disciples will eat the Passover, and he will guide you to an upper room in his house, furnished and prepared for this; there make ready the Passover. In faith they obeyed, and found it as He had told them, and prepared the Passover.

22.4.1.en: He did not mention that it was Mark so that Judas Iscariot would not know and tell the chief priests, because He wanted to complete the Passover and to institute the sacrament of Holy Communion before He was arrested.

22.4.2.en: Obedience makes it easy for a person to order all his life, so obey God's commandments and you will find rest.

22.5.s.en: (4) The Passover and the Lord's Supper

22.5.0.en: When the hour came to eat the Passover, which according to the Law is between the two evenings, that is, between the third and fifth hours in the afternoon, Christ reclined with His disciples to eat the Passover, and this was contrary to the custom of the Jews, who ate it standing. The Lord had commanded this so that they would remember their bondage in the land of Egypt, but now that Christ had come to free them by His death for them, He seated them around Him as sons and not as slaves.

22.6.0.en: Christ desired to eat this Passover with His disciples, because it was the last time He would eat a meal with them on earth, as a religious love feast with its spiritual symbols, which are fulfilled in His life-giving Cross, and from which is founded the sacrament of His most holy Body and Blood, which He declares and gives to His children on the same day after eating this Passover.

22.7.0.en: I will not drink of the fruit of the vine: I will not drink wine with you on earth a second time, for this is the last Passover He keeps with them.

22.7.1.en: Until the kingdom of God shall come: the heavenly Kingdom, where we are satisfied spiritually with Christ in heaven. Christ declares that He will not eat of this Passover again on earth, and that He will eat it with His disciples and all who believe in Him when their salvation is completed on the Cross, and He will satisfy them forever in His Kingdom. For Christ is our Passover and our spiritual food, not only by His Body and Blood in the Church, but in eternity He is the satisfaction of all His children... this is the fulfillment of the Passover in heaven.

22.7.2.en: This cup is one of the cups of wine that they drink with the Passover, and it is implicitly understood that He tasted it and then gave it to His disciples after giving thanks, according to the custom of the Jews. And He repeats that this is the last time He keeps the Passover and drinks of its wine until He drinks it spiritually in the eternal Kingdom. For wine signifies joy, and His joy is completed by the salvation of all His children and their entering the Kingdom, and that after the day of the last resurrection.

22.8.0.en: Here Christ institutes the sacrament of the Eucharist, that is, thanksgiving. He took bread other than the food of the Passover, and gave thanks, and broke it, and gave it to the disciples to eat, declaring that this is His true Body which He gives on the Cross, and He requires His Apostles and all His Church to do this sacrament always, to remember His love and the giving of His life on the Cross. The remembrance is not of a story that happened long ago, but is concrete, that is, a true Body and true Blood, as He made clear in (Jn 6:53-56).

22.8.1.en: And after giving them His Body to eat, He took a new cup other than the cups of the Passover and gave it to them to drink, declaring that the wine in it had been changed into His Blood, which He sheds on the Cross for the salvation of the world. Christ made the Lord's Supper, that is, instituted the sacrament of Holy Communion, immediately after the Passover, to declare that the Passover is a type of partaking of His Body and Blood.

22.9.0.en: Christ declared a bitter truth, which is that one of His disciples would betray Him and deliver Him to the Jews, for He said, "the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table," that is, one of the disciples at the table of the Passover. St. Luke does not care about chronological order, for Christ said these words after the Passover and before the institution of the sacrament of the Eucharist, as the other Gospels relate.

22.9.1.en: And Christ shows the heinousness of this man's sin (Judas Iscariot): Christ is not troubled by His sufferings and crucifixion, for they are necessary in His plan and must be accomplished, but this does not cancel the hideousness of Judas's betrayal and the punishment awaiting him in eternity. These words stirred grief and perplexity in the disciples' hearts, and they asked who this betraying disciple was.

22.9.2.en: As it was determined: Christ decided to die for the redemption of mankind, so He will surely die, but woe to the betrayer who sells his Master, for Christ's bearing of sufferings does not cancel the wickedness of Judas.

22.9.3.en: God warns us of our sins so that we do not fall into them, so would that we heed His warnings and repent quickly.

22.10.0.en: Christ was preparing for His sufferings to redeem mankind whom He loves, while the chief priests were consulting with envy and malice how to arrest Him and kill Him; and His closest ones, the disciples, were preoccupied, instead of sharing His sufferings, with seeking who among them was the greatest, who would take a greater place in the earthly kingdom that they thought Christ would set up. Opinions differed and a dispute arose among the disciples, each of them seeking how to be greater and more important than the others.

22.11.0.en: Christ understood what had passed among His disciples and reproved them for their love of preeminence, since this vice is one of the traits of the Gentiles far from God, who seek greatness and give gifts in order that people may call them benefactors and generous, and by this they lord it over one another.

22.11.1.en: But among those who believe in Christ, whoever is greater in age or position or knowledge, and so on, should make himself smaller and less than the rest, and whoever has the ability to lead and to go ahead should deal as a servant to all. Therefore in the Church of the New Testament, whoever teaches another and leads him in the way of the spiritual life is called a servant, to remember always to put himself lower than all.

22.12.0.en: Christ presented Himself as an example of humility, for He, the Teacher, who ought to sit while His disciples serve Him, was concerned to serve them, even to wash their feet. He washed His disciples' feet after the Passover and before the institution of the sacrament of Holy Communion. This quarrel either happened after the washing of the feet or happened before entering Jerusalem, but Luke mentioned it later because he does not care about the chronological order of events. To them.

22.13.0.en: Continued with me in my temptations: they left their families, and bore the insults and enmity of the scribes and Pharisees. I appoint unto you a kingdom: I give you the heavenly Kingdom as a reward for what you have endured.

22.13.1.en: As my Father hath appointed unto me: that is, Christ has His kingdom from eternity, which He has in the Father, and He emptied Himself by the Incarnation and took the form of an ordinary man, and then returns to His glory after His resurrection and ascension.

22.13.2.en: That ye may eat and drink... in my kingdom: spiritual satisfaction with Christ in the Kingdom of Heaven. It also means God's reign over the hearts of the disciples by faith in the Church, so that they partake of His Body and Blood all their lives on earth.

22.13.3.en: On thrones: this shows the greatness of the disciples' standing in the Kingdom of Heaven.

22.13.4.en: Christ praises His disciples because they bore with Him the sufferings of service, leaving their families and homes, and He promises them the eternal Kingdom with Him, and that they will eat at the spiritual table in heaven and enjoy His fellowship forever. And in this place of theirs they will judge all the Jews who did not believe in Him, for the Jews will look at His disciples in the glory they obtained because of their faith, and will regret it in eternal torment because they were with them in the same circumstances and did not believe. Put others before yourself in honor, and if you take a leading position, praise and lift up those with you, seeking in your heart what is more important, which is fellowship with God, and you will receive happiness on earth and joy in heaven.

22.14.0.en: Here Christ calls Simon by his old name, which means the weak, and not Peter, the strong rock, the name Christ gave him, because Satan seized the opportunity of Christ's entering into His sufferings and aimed his arrows at the disciples to show their weakness, and even to sift them as wheat. This was by God's permission, so that when their personal weakness appeared they would be humbled, and He would support them by His Holy Spirit, and their faith and their clinging to Him would increase.

22.15.0.en: That thy faith fail not: even if you fall through the weakness of your faith, your faith will not vanish, but you will rise, repent and return to God.

22.15.1.en: Strengthen thy brethren: this shows the weakness of the disciples and the exposure of all of them to doubting and denial like Peter, and their need to have their faith strengthened.

22.15.2.en: Christ comes forward in humility to pray for us, showing His love and fatherhood. And He speaks here as a man although He is God who is able to do all things, to teach us humility, love and prayer for others.

22.15.3.en: Then an important spiritual meaning appears, which is that the penitent, once he has turned from his sins, ought to do a positive work: he calls souls to Christ and strengthens them in the faith, as Christ asked Peter, when he repented, to strengthen his brethren. For the penitent feels for sinners like himself, and so he is tender toward them and encourages them.

22.15.4.en: Take care to live the life of repentance, so that you are a true servant who gathers souls to Christ and not merely a teacher of lifeless teachings.

22.16.0.en: This discourse is mentioned in (Mt 26:33-35). Here the impetuosity of Simon Peter appears, which came from love but without prudence, for he promised not to leave Christ even to prison and death, forgetting his weakness and his need of God's support. For this reason Christ directed the discourse to him before the rest of the disciples, to teach him and them humility, repentance and reliance on God's help.

22.17.0.en: Christ called Simon by this name although He had named him a rock, that is, Peter, but he would weaken and deny Him three times, and He gave him a sign, which is the crowing of the cock after this denial. The cock confesses the name of God by its familiar voice, but Peter the man denies Christ and says, "I know him not." Christ also warned Peter against denying, saying in effect, you know Me, so beware of saying that you do not know Me, and despite this warning Peter denied Him. Beware of denying Christ by your sins which cause others to stumble, so that you become a curse upon His holy name.

22.18.0.en: Christ alerted His disciples to the principle of not depending on material things when going out to serve, which they applied when they served in Judea; but now, as they prepare to preach in the whole world Christ crucified and risen from the dead, they need spiritual striving with all their energies, which He indicated by the purse and the scrip, that is, all their resources. What is meant is not reliance on money and stored food for going out to serve, but spiritual striving of prayers, fasts and prostrations, perseverance in teaching and persuading others, and all the gifts that God gives to servants.

22.18.1.en: Then He says that whoever has no abilities and gifts and feels weakness, let him sell his garment, meaning let him live in detachment and asceticism even from necessities, and in prayers and fasts, and leave the comfort of the body and buy the sword of the Spirit... that is, hold fast to the word of God.

22.19.0.en: That which is written (Isa 53:12): "He was numbered with the transgressors": His crucifixion between two thieves.

22.19.1.en: Have an end: I shall accomplish the redemption and rise from the dead.

22.19.2.en: Here Christ affirms the necessity of His bearing the sufferings, the crucifixion and death, for this is necessary for the redemption of mankind and will end at the appointed time, that is, the time of the Cross; and then He rises from the dead and gives the Holy Spirit to His children, so that they preach Him in the whole world.

22.20.0.en: The disciples did not understand Christ's spiritual meaning, which is striving with the sword of the Spirit, and they thought He was speaking of a material battle in which they would gather money and swords for war, as appears from the literal meaning of the words, so they answered Him that they had two swords. And of course these were a group of fishermen who had not been trained in the use of swords, and it is said that they were not two swords but two large knives which they had used in eating the Passover.

22.20.1.en: And Christ replied to them that it was enough, that is, enough talk on this subject, because they did not understand His meaning, and He does not mean that two swords are enough for a material battle, as shown by His rebuke of Peter when he tried to use his sword to cut off the ear of the high priest's servant at the arrest of Christ). Mt 26:52) If you are fighting a repeated or increasing sin, you need to use all your spiritual weapons, and because of your striving God has compassion on you and lifts these wars from you.

22.21.0.en: Went out: from the city of Jerusalem.

22.21.1.en: The Mount of Olives: at its foot is the garden of Gethsemane, which He entered.

22.21.2.en: Christ was accustomed to go to a garden on the Mount of Olives with His disciples. Some say that it belonged to Mark the Apostle, and He went to it after eating the Passover and the Lord's Supper.

22.22.0.en: When they arrived at the garden on the mountain, He called His disciples to pray, since they were about to face hard events, which were seeing their Teacher arrested and then crucified, and their exposure to fear and doubt and all the wars the devil had prepared for them; for prayer protects them from falling into temptation and turning away from God. However hard your circumstances, trust that your prayers and your clinging to God will carry you through the affliction in peace without falling into sin.

22.23.0.en: A stone's cast: about 20 meters, a near distance that allowed the three disciples to see Him and hear Him.

22.23.1.en: Christ left eight of His disciples at the entrance of the garden, and moved away from them with the remaining three, and then went into the depth of the garden a distance of about 20 meters, to be alone in prayer, and each group praying together.

22.24.0.en: Christ knelt down as a man, declaring the weight of the coming sufferings, not only the bodily sufferings on the Cross but also the psychological ones, by the denial and withdrawal of the disciples from Him and the standing of the crowds He had served demanding His crucifixion, and also the spiritual sufferings in bearing all the sins of men while He is the Righteous One. Therefore He asked in prayer, as a man, that the cup of suffering pass from Him, for it was very heavy, but at the same time He carries out the highest training in Christianity, which is surrendering the will to God, so He says, "not my will, but thine, be done." And though He is perfect God and knows that He will complete the bearing of the Cross, He showed that He has a perfect humanity that suffers pain. And He prayed this prayer three times, for He would return to His three disciples and find them asleep and wake them to pray and go back and pray alone, as the Gospel of Matthew relates.

22.24.1.en: Ask God's help and the lifting of the affliction from you, but in the end accept His will, for it is your good even if you do not see that at present, but believe in His good ordering of your life.

22.25.0.en: Heaven responded to Christ who suffered for us, but mankind was preparing death for Him, and even those nearest to Him, His disciples, did not stand with Him but were overcome by sleep.

22.25.1.en: And here the love of the angels for men appears, for an angel came to strengthen Christ as a man, to show their readiness to help men in all their afflictions.

22.26.0.en: Christ continued in fervent prayer, feeling all the sufferings coming upon Him, and His sweat was as it were great drops of blood, that is, pressed out by sorrow (the word Gethsemane means a press).

22.26.1.en: Persevere in your prayers however hard the affliction or however delayed the answer, for God cares greatly about every word and tear and drop of sweat in your prayer.

22.27.0.en: After His prayer Christ went back to look at His disciples and found them heavy with sleep, for they were sorrowful at what they had heard from Him about the sufferings coming upon Him, so Christ roused them to wake and continue in prayer so that temptation would not overcome them.

22.28.0.en: After Christ's prayers in the garden of Gethsemane and His discourse with His disciples about the importance of prayer as protection from falling into temptations, Judas Iscariot, a disciple of Christ, came, and with him a crowd of chief priests, captains of the temple guard and some soldiers with torches, swords and staves to arrest Christ, and the agreed sign was that whomever Judas kissed they would seize.

22.29.0.en: The betrayal of Christ by Judas was utterly heinous, because without cause the disciple who clung to his Teacher betrays Him and sells Him to His enemies at the lowest of prices, the price of a slave, thirty pieces of silver. Despite Judas's wickedness, Christ still loved him, so He rebukes him in case he seizes the last chance and repents, saying to him how he uses the means of expressing love, the kiss, for betrayal and evil and the killing of others, indeed the killing of his Master and Teacher, the one who had done everything for him and who came for his salvation and the salvation of all mankind.

22.29.1.en: And on the other hand, how can he deliver to death Christ, the Son of man, the Righteous One who never sinned.

22.30.0.en: Peter, and with him the rest of the disciples, asked Christ, "Shall we smite with the sword?", that is, shall they use their swords to defend Him?

22.30.1.en: For they had understood His earlier words about buying swords to mean a material battle in which they would defend Christ with these swords. And Peter rushed in, without waiting for Christ's answer, and cut off the right ear of the high priest's servant, because he was a fisherman and did not know how to use swords, or even knives. The Evangelists did not mention the names of the striker and the struck except John alone, because he wrote his Gospel at the end of the first century after the martyrdom of Peter the Apostle, since there was no longer any fear of the Roman authority rebuking him for trying to kill the high priest's servant (Jn 18:10).

22.31.0.en: Here the divinity of Christ and His wonderful love for His enemies appear, for He touched the severed ear and it was healed at once, declaring that His battle is with the spiritual hosts of evil and not with men, and He defeats them by His death on the Cross and binds Satan.

22.31.1.en: And His healing of the high priest's servant was to stop the soldiers from arresting or harming His disciples, especially Peter, who cut off the servant's ear. Sadly those who came to arrest Him were not affected by this miracle, and continued in the hardness of their hearts and arrested Him to kill Him.

22.31.2.en: Offer your love to all, even to your enemies, and declare the truth and rebuke them if they listen to you, that perhaps they will repent and return to God.

22.32.0.en: Captains of the temple: the Levites responsible for guarding the temple, who were under the chief priests.

22.32.1.en: The elders: the elders of the Jews who were esteemed among the people.

22.32.2.en: Your hour: the time that God permitted for Him to offer Himself to die for the world.

22.32.3.en: The power of darkness: the power of evil which the devil moves to harm everyone who does good.

22.32.4.en: Christ showed His love for the crowd that came to arrest Him by alerting them to the evil they were doing... It is astonishing that they came as a large group armed with swords and staves to arrest Him as though He were a dangerous criminal fleeing from justice, though He is the good Teacher who preached every day in the temple to save all. But He declares God's permission that the devil should have power and stir up their malice to arrest Him and kill Him.

22.32.5.en: Take heed lest you rush into wronging another although he is innocent.

22.33.0.en: When they had arrested Christ, they led Him to be tried at the house of Caiaphas the high priest, after they had first tried Him at the house of Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas.

22.34.0.en: While Christ was being tried inside the house of Caiaphas the high priest, Peter sat in the midst of the hall, that is, a little way from the place of Christ's trial, and around Peter was a group of maidservants and servants who had kindled a fire because the weather was cold at night.

22.35.0.en: As Peter was sitting, one of the maidservants noticed that he had been one of those close to Christ during His teachings and miracles among the crowds, and she declared this to all around, but Peter denied, pretending that he did not know Christ Jesus.

22.36.0.en: After a short while one of those in the hall noticed Peter, and said to all that this man was one of the followers of Christ, and Peter denied a second time.

22.36.1.en: The trial continued, and after about an hour a third person noticed Peter and his speech with the accent of the Galileans, and declared this before all, but Peter denied for the third time that he knew Christ, and immediately after that the cock crew, and this was the sign Christ had mentioned to Peter when He warned him that he would deny Him.

22.37.0.en: The trials did not distract Jesus from the salvation of Peter's soul, for when the cock crew Christ left everyone and looked at Peter who was sitting outside. He looked with the rebuke of love to alert him to the sin into which he had fallen so that he would repent, and Peter could not bear the love of Christ shining upon him from His eyes, so he went outside the house and wept bitterly, feeling his weakness and ingratitude in denying the loving Christ who had cared for him for more than three years. Despite the heinousness of Peter's sin, the tears of his repentance and deep remorse were his way back to God. Repentance is the shortest road to the heart of God, the tender and forgiving, however great your sins.

22.38.0.en: After Christ's second trial, they scourged Him with 39 stripes according to the Roman law, and they were not content with harming Him bodily but also psychologically, by mocking Him and jeering at Him.

22.39.0.en: Among the ways of mocking Him, they covered His face and began to strike Him, then lifted the covering and asked Him to prophesy who had struck Him, if He knew the hidden things as they say of Him.

22.40.0.en: They continued mocking Him as a sinner and criminal, though He is the Righteous and Holy One who bore in silence all their reproaches.

22.40.1.en: It is hard to bear insults without sinning, especially from those younger than you or lower in position, but remember what the King of kings and Lord of lords bore.

22.41.0.en: As soon as it was day: the Law provides that no one be sentenced to death except in the daytime, so they were not content with the night trials, and the supreme council of the Jews, the Sanhedrin, that is, the seventy elders, assembled in the daytime to try Christ for the third time.

22.41.1.en: They brought Christ to the third trial in their council, where the chief priests and the scribes, who are the elders esteemed among the Jews, were gathered, and they asked Him whether He was the Christ, and He answered them that they were unwilling to believe His words, for they had seen His miracles and heard His teachings before and rejected them out of their envy and wickedness, and that whatever He said to them they would not release Him, because they were insistent on killing Him and were looking only for evidence and a reason to complete their crime.

22.42.0.en: When Christ felt their inability to find a charge against Him, He gave them a ground on which to rely in killing Him, for He told them that the hour had drawn near for the Son of man to sit on the right hand of the power of God, that is, to regain His divine glory in heaven. He here repeats what He declared in His trial before Caiaphas, which took place at night (Mt 26:64).

22.43.0.en: So they asked Him to be certain of the meaning of His words whether He meant that He was the Son of God, and Christ affirmed this to them as they spoke and said. And so Christ declared His divinity plainly so that whoever wishes may believe in Him, and these words of His would be a judgment on whoever does not believe and on whoever dares to crucify Him and kill Him.

22.43.1.en: Christ reveals Himself to you however deep you are sunk in sin, that perhaps you will take heed and repent.

22.44.0.en: The ignorant Jews thought they had found tangible evidence to condemn Him and crucify Him, and did not understand that the wise Christ, whom they had not been able to catch with a single word throughout all their former plots, is the one who declared His divinity, bearing their malice and their use of these words of His to kill Him.

22.44.1.en: The three official trials, the crucifixion and death: the events in this chapter are mentioned in (Mt 27; Mk 15; Jn 18:28 to the end of ch. 19). His trial before Pilate (vv. 1-7):

22.44.2.en: 1- And the whole multitude of them arose, and led him unto Pilate. 2- And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ a King." 3- And Pilate asked him, saying, "Art thou the King of the Jews?" And he answered him and said, "Thou sayest it." 4- Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, "I find no fault in this man." 5- And they were the more fierce, saying, "He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place." 6- When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.

22.44.3.en: 7- And as soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time.
